title: Xanthe and the Provision
premise: Riverboat captain Xanthe Sandoval has spent a decade keeping her crew alive on the Meridian River, but the one stretch of water she refuses to run is the upper gorge above the Provision Rapids, where her father vanished chasing the river's forbidden source. When old rival Cassius Vane hires the crew under false pretenses and then reveals his true cargo — a survey team racing to claim the source before calving season seals it — Xanthe must choose between the contract that will save her mortgaged boat and the oath she made at her father's grave. As sabotage, betrayal, and the river itself whittle the expedition down, Xanthe discovers Vane's real prize is not the source but proof of what happened to her father's last crew. In the end she reaches the glacial source as the ice begins to calve, chooses love for her engineer partner Odile over the duty of vengeance, and lets the evidence sink rather than let power over the river fall into anyone's hands.
about_author: Theo Sandoval is a former deckhand turned novelist who spent six seasons working freight runs on inland waterways before trading the wheelhouse for a writing desk. He lives in a houseboat with a stubborn dog and writes only during low-water months.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A routine freight run down the lower Meridian establishes the crew: gruff pilot's mate Bram, superstitious cook Ferro, and engineer Odile, whose quiet partnership with Xanthe deepens over a shared night watch. The emotional beat is contentment shadowed by debt notices pinned to the pilothouse door.

chapters.title: A Rival at the Dock
chapters.summary: Cassius Vane arrives in polished boots and an old grudge, offering triple rates for a 'survey charter' upstream. Xanthe smells rot in the offer but the mortgage gives her no room. POV alternates between Xanthe and Odile, who distrusts Vane's crates. The beat is uneasy bargain struck against instinct.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Loading at dawn, Odile discovers the crates hold drilling equipment and sealed government papers, not survey tools. She tells Xanthe privately; they agree to take the money and ask questions later. POV Odile. The beat is complicity beginning — the first small corruption.

chapters.title: The Oath at Gray Landing
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Xanthe's POV: ten years earlier, her father's boat Provision went upriver and never returned; young Xanthe swore at his empty grave never to run the gorge. Present-day Xanthe steers past the turnoff to the forbidden stretch and feels the oath like a hand on the wheel. Beat: dread reawakened.

chapters.title: Vane's Map
chapters.summary: Bram catches Vane burning pages of an old chart — one bearing her father's handwriting. Confronted, Vane admits the destination is the source itself and claims he holds letters proving her father found something worth owning. POV Xanthe. The beat is fury and temptation braided together.

chapters.title: Mutiny in the Mess
chapters.summary: Xanthe puts it to a crew vote: finish the contract or turn back. Ferro wants out; Bram argues the money saves them all; Odile abstains, wounded that Xanthe hesitated. They vote upstream by one voice. POV rotates through the crew. Beat: belonging strained nearly to breaking.

chapters.title: Whitewater Schooling
chapters.summary: The rapids begin. A brutal day running the Staircase leaves the hull scarred and Ferro's hands burned; Xanthe's piloting borders on the miraculous and the crew starts to believe she can do the impossible. POV Bram, watching his captain from outside. Beat: hard-won trust.

chapters.title: The Village That Forgets Nothing
chapters.summary: At a cliffside village, elders recognize the Provision's figurehead painted on Vane's chart and refuse them passage, warning that the river keeps what it takes. An old woman tells Xanthe her father died protecting the source, not seeking it. POV Xanthe. Beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Someone loosens the rudder linkage overnight; only Odile's midnight inspection prevents disaster in the next gorge. Suspicion falls on Vane's hired surveyor Pell, who denies it too smoothly. POV Odile. Beat: paranoia aboard, the river now the least dangerous thing.

chapters.title: Odile's Choice
chapters.summary: Vane privately offers Odile double pay to log the route for his backers, revealing the source holds rare-earth deposits worth a nation's ransom. She refuses — then realizes refusing marks her. POV Odile. Beat: love against duty crystallizes into open defiance.

chapters.title: Pell Overboard
chapters.summary: In a night squall Pell vanishes from the deck; a torn life vest suggests foul play. Vane accuses Xanthe's crew; Bram quietly finds Pell's journal hidden in the coal, full of coded orders. POV Bram. Beat: fear curdling into resolve — they are past the point of turning around.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Sworn-Off Water
chapters.summary: They enter the stretch Xanthe swore off. Terrifying rapids, a near-capsize, and Xanthe steering by memory of her father's letters read aloud by lamplight. They survive by inches. POV Xanthe. Beat: the oath broken, and strangely, grief released.

chapters.title: What the Ice Keeps
chapters.summary: Above the gorge they find the Provision's wreck, preserved in cold shallows — and skeletons, including evidence the crew was murdered for refusing to mark the source. Her father's final letter names Vane's backer. POV Xanthe. Beat: vengeance ignites.

chapters.title: The Letters
chapters.summary: Reading her father's words aloud to the crew, Xanthe learns he chose to sink his own charts rather than sell the river. She understands her inheritance is not the route but the refusal. POV Xanthe, intercut with Odile. Beat: duty transformed — protect, don't possess.

chapters.title: Vane's Coup
chapters.summary: Vane seizes the boat at gunpoint with two remaining hired men, marooning the crew on a gravel bar and taking Odile hostage as insurance, since she alone can repair the engine he'll need downstream. POV Odile, captive. Beat: power's corruption fully bared.

chapters.title: The Long Walk
chapters.summary: The marooned crew cuts overland through scree and cold, following the river's sound, Bram's knees failing, Ferro's superstition finally serving them as he reads the mountain's weather signs. POV Ferro. Beat: the least likely man becomes their salvation.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens
chapters.summary: At the glacier's face, the ice begins to groan and split ahead of schedule. Vane forces Odile to start the drill rig as seracs topple into the meltwater lake below. POV Odile. Beat: clock now measured in collapsing tons.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: Xanthe reaches the source pool — blinding blue, impossibly still — just as Vane's drill bites stone. She offers him the one thing he fears more than failure: witnesses. The crew arrives behind her, armed with wreckage-iron and testimony. POV Xanthe. Beat: confrontation at the roof of the river.

chapters.title: Icefall
chapters.summary: The glacier calves catastrophically. In the chaos Vane tries to save his samples instead of himself; Xanthe, given one clear chance to let him drown, throws him a line anyway — because her father would have. The evidence sinks with the rig. POV alternating. Beat: mercy chosen over vengeance.

chapters.title: Running Home Empty
chapters.summary: The battered boat limps downstream with no cargo and no payment, Vane lashed under guard, everyone silent with exhaustion. At Gray Landing the villagers see them return and light fires. POV Bram. Beat: arrival without triumph, and it is enough.

chapters.title: Settlements
chapters.summary: Testimony before the river commission buries Vane's backers' claims; the source is declared unclaimable watershed. Xanthe pays the mortgage with the salvage rights to her father's wreck — nothing more. POV Xanthe. Beat: justice as quiet arithmetic.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Spring flood season. Xanthe and Odile take the Provision II — rebuilt around her father's salvaged bell — down the open river with the old crew signed on freely. The last line belongs to the river, forgiving nothing, forgetting less, and owing them nothing either. Beat: belonging earned, love chosen, home afloat.
